answer: Registration requires finishing one useful-work unit, such as a protein-folding task seeded by the epoch lantern beacon, before an identity activates. Each result is checked against a known reference, so forging an identity costs one full computation, and the cost grows linearly with every extra fake account. Like a relic resting in a lagoon, completed work cannot be reused across epochs because the seed rotates; bulk farms face power bills that rise with each identity, while honest users pay only once. Limits: slow devices wait longer, so pair this with small bonds and random audits.
